name: What is Object Storage?
description:
Object storage (also known as object-based storage) is a storage architecture that manages data as objects, as opposed to other storage architectures like file systems which manage data as a file hierarchy and block storage which manages data as blocks within sectors and tracks.

Each object typically includes the data itself, a variable amount of metadata, and a globally unique identifier. Objects could be your documents, photos, videos, music, disk image etc you can think of them as files on a file system

Object storage systems allow relatively inexpensive, scalable and self-healing retention of massive amounts of unstructured data. Object storage is used for diverse purposes such as storing photos on Facebook, songs on Spotify, or files in online collaboration services, such as Dropbox.

name: What's Swift?
description: The OpenStack Object Store project, known as Swift, offers cloud storage software so that you can store and retrieve lots of data with a simple API. It's built for scale and optimized for durability, availability, and concurrency across the entire data set. Swift is ideal for storing unstructured data that can grow without bound.

name: Install OpenStack DevStack
description:
We covered these steps on OpenStack basics under topic Install and Configure DevStack. And couple of time during Cinder and Glance. This time, we will run a wrapper script which will download the repo and setup config files. Just run the wrapper script after updating the system 
sudo apt-get update  
sudo apt-get -y install git

wget -O- http://giis.co.in/install_devstack.sh | bash

Enable Swift services

By default, swift uses port 8080, we will change this so that it works properly in webminal environment.
find port 8080 and change it as 8089 with simple find and sedcommand like
cd /home/stack/openstack
find . -type f -print0 | xargs -0 sed -i 's/8080/8089/g'
Just run below command to enable Swift services on config file
echo enable_service s-proxy s-object >> local.conf
echo enable_service s-container s-account >> local.conf
Okay done, please check the local.conf and openrc files. Lets run the devstack script, you know it will around ~30 minutes.

sudo su stack
cd ~
 /home/stack/openstack/stack.sh

name: Swift basic commands
description:
Swift client provides following basics commands:
  • stat → Displays account,container or object information.
  • list → Lists the containers or objects.
  • post → Updates meta information.
  • upload → Uploads files to the given container.
  • download → Download objects from containers.
  • delete → Delete a container or objects.
We will export OpenStack environment variables first:
source /home/stack/openstack/openrc
To Display information about account, container and object, type:
swift stat 

                                
        Account: AUTH_5b510a4ea4234eb1b6d07aaae965ab2e
     Containers: 0
        Objects: 0                               
          Bytes: 0                          
X-Put-Timestamp: 1444494578.35641                          
    X-Timestamp: 1444494578.35641                         
     X-Trans-Id: tx16be57e3f8544ec5ab281-0056193cf2            
   Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Since we yet to create any containers or objects , they are shown as empty/zero.

name: Container creation and Upload
description:
Normally, post will update the meta information of the container. If the container is not found, it will be created automatically.
swift post wmcontainer
Now run list command to lists the containers.
swift list 
  
wmcontainer
We will create file named file.txt and upload this into our Object-Storage container wmcontainer
echo "Uploaded this content" > file.txt
To upload this file into our container,type:
swift upload wmcontainer file.txt 
 file.txt
Verify the container objects using list command now.
swift list wmcontainer
Can you see the objects this time?

name: Download an object
description:
Lets download object from container
cd /tmp
swift download wmcontainer file.txt 
 file.txt [auth 0.378s, headers 0.474s, total 0.475s, 0.000 MB/s]

Verify the downloaded content with catcommand.

name: Upload and Download multiple objects
description:
We say uploading single file and download a file. How to upload or download more than one file? We will find the answer to this question here.
To upload multiple files use
swift upload wmcontainer file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt
Assuming you already created file2.txt and file3.txt.
To download multiple files simply use
swift download wmcontainer
 If you want to download the container itself then type
swift download --all
 Can you see the downloaded files?

name: Using Pseudo directory
description:
So far we uploaded files individually, don't you think it would be nice to have option to uploaded directory? Unforunately object doesn't have directories. but they do have something called 'pseudo directory' to mimic directory like layout.

Lets create a pseudo directory dir0 with file f1,f2

mkdir dir0

echo "new content under pseudo directory" > dir0/f1

echo "new content under pseudo directory" > dir0/f2
We can uploaded multiple files using this pseudo directory.
swift upload wmcontainer dir0

name: Delete Object and Container
description:
Lets say we want to cleanup pseudo directory for some reason.
swift delete wmcontainer dir0
Now go Horizon or use swift list command to verify these changes.
We can also remove the container itself by running below command.
swift delete wmcontainer
Again please verify :)
